2026-120.plain: The House voted 224 to 204 to pass a bill directing the Department of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status for 18 months starting August 3, 2025. That status would allow eligible Haitian nationals to obtain work authorization, protect them from detention based on immigration status, and shield them from removal while they keep the status.

2026-121.name: Resolution Supporting Tax Policies for Working Families
2026-121.plain: The House voted 219 to 207 to approve a resolution expressing support for tax policies that help working families and recognizing tax relief enacted in 2025. Nearly all Republicans voted yes, and nearly all Democrats voted no.

2026-123.name: Extending Foreign Surveillance Authority Through 2027
2026-123.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to a bill that would extend certain foreign intelligence surveillance powers through October 20, 2027. The amendment failed, 200 in favor to 220 against.

2026-125.name: Faster Broadband Permit Reviews on Public Land
2026-125.plain: The House voted 384 to 9 to pass a bill creating a federal team to speed up reviews of requests to build or change communications equipment on public lands. The team would set review goals and report to Congress on how well it works.

2026-126.name: Emergency Reporting Act
2026-126.plain: The House voted to pass a bill requiring the Federal Communications Commission to study 9-1-1 outages and communication failures during disasters, hold yearly public hearings, and publish reports with recommendations. The bill passed 386 to 7.

2026-127.name: Kari's Law Reporting Act
2026-127.plain: The House voted 405 to 5 to pass a bill requiring the Federal Communications Commission to publish a report on how well manufacturers have followed Kari's Law, which lets people dial 9-1-1 directly from multiline office phones, and to recommend any needed improvements.

2026-128.name: Rural Health Care Funding Extension
2026-128.plain: The House passed a bill, 406 to 4, to extend through 2030 federal grants that help health care providers and networks serve rural areas. It also requires that the grant money meet the needs of underserved groups and involve them in planning.

2026-129.name: Hydropower Project Construction Deadline Extension
2026-129.plain: The House passed a bill, 394 to 14, that lets federal regulators give hydropower projects licensed before March 2020 more time to start construction, up to six additional years beyond current limits. It also lets regulators reinstate certain expired licenses for those projects.

2026-13.name: Remote Access Security Act
2026-13.plain: The House passed the Remote Access Security Act, 369 to 22. The bill would extend U.S. export controls to foreign people who remotely use controlled items, such as through the internet or cloud computing, and let the Commerce Department issue licenses and impose penalties for that access.

2026-132.name: Support for Rural Communities Resolution
2026-132.plain: The House voted 220 to 196 to approve a resolution expressing support for rural communities across the United States and recognizing the House's work on their behalf. Passed.

2026-134.name: Federal Building Energy Standards Rollback
2026-134.plain: The House passed a bill, 215 to 202, that would repeal rules phasing out fossil fuel use in new and major-renovation federal buildings by 2030. It would also bar green-building certification systems from denying federal buildings certification solely because of fossil fuel use.

2026-136.name: FIRE Act on Air Quality and Wildfires
2026-136.plain: The House passed the FIRE Act, 220 to 198. The bill changes how the Clean Air Act treats pollution caused by wildfire-prevention work and certain high-heat or dry weather, and it requires the EPA to update its rules for handling that air data.

2026-137.name: HEATS Act on Geothermal Energy Permits
2026-137.plain: The House passed the HEATS Act, 231 to 186. The bill would let certain geothermal energy projects on state and private land skip federal drilling permits and federal environmental and historic preservation reviews, if the operator has a state permit.

2026-138.name: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act
2026-138.plain: The House passed a bill, 346 to 10, changing how the IRS handles rewards and protections for people who report tax cheating. Under the bill, whistleblowers could stay anonymous in tax court cases, and the IRS would owe interest if it is late in notifying a whistleblower about an award.

2026-139.name: Clergy Act: Opting Back Into Social Security and Medicare
2026-139.plain: The House passed the Clergy Act, 350 to 5, using a fast-track process that does not allow amendments. The bill gives members of the clergy who previously opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes a two-year window to opt back in.

2026-14.name: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
2026-14.plain: The House passed this bill, 340 to 54, to keep federal agencies funded at current levels through December 11, 2026, so a shutdown is avoided, and to extend several expiring programs, including grain inspection, cybersecurity information sharing, and trade benefits for African countries.

2026-142.name: Foreign Surveillance Law and Central Bank Digital Currency Ban
2026-142.plain: The House passed a bill extending a foreign intelligence surveillance law until 2029, adding limits on FBI searches of Americans' communications, and barring the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency. The vote was 235 in favor and 191 against.

2026-143.name: Congressional Budget Plan for 2026
2026-143.plain: The House voted 215 to 211 to approve a budget resolution setting federal spending and revenue targets for fiscal year 2026 and later years through 2035. It also directs House and Senate committees to propose changes that would add no more than $70 billion to the deficit.

2026-144.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-144.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which covers farm programs like crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, 210 in favor to 216 against.

2026-145.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-145.plain: The House voted 384 to 35 to add an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, the farm bill. The bill would reauthorize farm and food programs through 2031, covering areas such as crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, rural development, and crop insurance.

2026-146.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-146.plain: The House voted 416 to 8 to add an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, the farm bill. The bill covers farm support, conservation, food aid, nutrition assistance, rural programs, crop insurance, and foreign purchases of U.S. farmland.

2026-147.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-147.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which covers farm programs, nutrition assistance, conservation, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, 69 in favor and 355 against.

2026-148.name: Amendment to the Farm Bill
2026-148.plain: The House voted 280 to 142 to add an amendment to the farm bill, which sets Department of Agriculture programs for crop support, conservation, nutrition, rural development, crop insurance, and foreign ownership of U.S. farmland through 2031.

2026-149.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-149.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which covers farm programs, food and nutrition assistance, conservation, and crop insurance. The amendment failed, 187 in favor to 239 against.

2026-15.name: Haiti Economic Lift Program Extension
2026-15.plain: The House voted 345 to 45 to pass a bill extending through 2028 the duty-free tariff rules for certain apparel imported from Haiti. It also directs refunds of duties paid on such imports entered after September 30, 2025.

2026-150.name: Amendment to the Farm Bill
2026-150.plain: The House voted to add an amendment to the farm bill, which covers farm programs, food and nutrition assistance, conservation, rural development, and crop insurance. The change was approved, 233 to 194.

2026-151.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-151.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, which covers farm programs, food and nutrition assistance, conservation, and rural development. The amendment failed, 186 to 238.

2026-152.name: Farm Bill Amendment
2026-152.plain: The House voted 215 to 213 to add an amendment to the farm bill, which renews Department of Agriculture programs through 2031 covering crop support, conservation, food aid, nutrition, farm credit, rural development, crop insurance, and foreign ownership of U.S. farmland.

2026-154.name: Farm Bill
2026-154.plain: The House passed the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 by 224 to 200. The bill renews federal farm and food programs through 2031, covering crop support, conservation, nutrition assistance, rural development, crop insurance, and foreign investment in U.S. farmland.

2026-155.name: Extension of Foreign Surveillance Law
2026-155.plain: The House passed a bill extending for about a year, until June 12, 2026, rules for government surveillance of communications from people believed to be outside the United States. The vote was 261 in favor and 111 against.

2026-156.name: Save Our Shrimpers Act
2026-156.plain: The House passed the Save Our Shrimpers Act, 391 to 18. The bill would bar federal funds from going to international financial institutions for financing foreign shrimp farming, processing, or exporting, and would require a yearly government report on U.S. leaders' compliance with rules opposing certain commodity financing.

2026-157.name: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
2026-157.plain: The House passed a bill to expand federal enforcement against organized theft from stores and shipments, including money laundering charges tied to stolen goods and gift cards, and to create a temporary Homeland Security center to coordinate these cases. The vote was 348 in favor and 60 against.

2026-161.name: Procedural Rule for Farm Bill and Fuel Retailer Measure
2026-161.plain: The House voted 213 to 208 to approve a resolution that removes a requirement tying the text of a fuel retailer choice bill to the farm bill. Both bills were then set up for House consideration.

2026-162.name: Honoring Law Enforcement Officers Killed in the Line of Duty
2026-162.plain: The House approved a resolution expressing support for police and other law enforcement officers and condolences to families of those killed on duty, passing 418 to 2. The measure does not create any new law or spending.

2026-164.name: Year-Round Sales of Higher-Ethanol Gasoline
2026-164.plain: The House passed a bill, 218 to 203, that would let gasoline with up to 15% ethanol be sold year-round, and would require the EPA to return some compliance credits to small refineries under certain conditions.

2026-165.name: Resolution Supporting Law Enforcement Officers
2026-165.plain: The House approved a resolution expressing support for law enforcement officers and recognizing their contributions and sacrifices, by a vote of 243 to 173.

2026-166.name: Resolution Countering Antisemitism
2026-166.plain: The House voted 419 to 0 to approve a resolution calling on leaders to condemn and counter antisemitism, honor Jewish-American service members, and commit to letting all Americans worship without fear of violence or persecution.

2026-167.name: Urging Release of Detained Religious and Political Figures in China
2026-167.plain: The House voted 414 to 0 to approve a non-binding resolution asking the President to press for the humanitarian release of five people detained in China, including two pastors and Jimmy Lai, during future talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. It also asks for proof they are alive, access to lawyers and family, and medical care.

2026-169.name: Bail Bond Insurance Fraud Bill
2026-169.plain: The House passed a bill 243 to 179 that would treat bail payments, including bail bonds and immigration bail bonds, as insurance business under federal law. This would make such bail providers subject to federal insurance fraud crimes and state insurance licensing and regulation.

2026-170.name: Ending U.S. Military Action Against Iran
2026-170.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran by March 30, 2026, unless Congress authorizes the action. It would not stop defensive actions against imminent attacks. The measure failed on a 212 to 212 tie.

2026-171.name: Cashless Bail Reporting Act
2026-171.plain: The House passed the Cashless Bail Reporting Act, 308 to 116. The bill would require the Justice Department to publish a yearly list of state and local governments that let people charged with certain serious offenses, such as burglary, murder, rape, looting, or vandalism, be released before trial without cash bail.

2026-173.name: Monitor Accountability Act
2026-173.plain: The House passed the Monitor Accountability Act, 219 to 204. The bill would require courts to set rules for monitors who oversee state and local governments under settlement agreements, including public notice before appointment, a five-year term limit, public reporting of fees, and a fee cap.

2026-174.name: Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Spending Bill
2026-174.plain: The House voted on adding a change to a bill that provides funding for military construction, Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the 2027 fiscal year. The change was rejected, 333 to 80.

2026-175.name: Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Funding
2026-175.plain: The House passed a bill providing funding for military construction, veterans programs, and related agencies for the 2027 fiscal year, by a vote of 400 to 15.

2026-176.name: Approval of Senate Changes to a Bill
2026-176.plain: The House voted 396 to 13 to approve changes the Senate made to a bill, which then goes on to the next step. The vote needed two-thirds support under a fast-track process, and it passed.

2026-177.name: Keeping Deposits Local Act
2026-177.plain: The House voted to pass a bill that would let banks accept a larger amount of reciprocal deposits, which are split across a network of banks to keep them fully insured, and would change the health ratings banks need to qualify. The bill passed 405 to 0.

2026-178.name: American Access to Banking Act
2026-178.plain: The House voted to pass a bill asking federal regulators to review and speed up the process for starting new banks and credit unions, including helping applicants with caseworkers and mentors. The measure passed 405 to 4.

2026-179.name: Community Bank Deposit Access Act
2026-179.plain: The House passed a bill, 393 to 16, that would stop certain custodial deposits at smaller community banks from being classed as brokered deposits, so those banks face less extra oversight. The bill was considered under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2026-180.name: Veterans Medical Facility Project in St. Louis
2026-180.plain: The House voted 405 to 5 to pass a bill allowing the Department of Veterans Affairs to build a major medical facility in St. Louis, Missouri, including a new bed tower, clinic expansion, administrative building, utility plant, and parking garages, with a set maximum spending limit.

2026-181.name: Lulu's Law on Shark Attack Phone Alerts
2026-181.plain: The House passed Lulu's Law by 401 votes to 6, using a fast-track process that skips amendments. The bill would require the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order allowing emergency alerts to be sent to mobile phones when a shark attack occurs.

2026-182.name: 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Commemorative Coin
2026-182.plain: The House passed a bill directing the Treasury to mint commemorative coins marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks and the National September 11 Memorial and Museum. Sales of the coins would include a surcharge going to the memorial and museum, unless annual issuance limits are exceeded. The vote was 415 in favor and none opposed.

2026-184.name: Parental Consent for School Gender Changes Bill
2026-184.plain: The House passed the bill 217 to 198. It would require public elementary and middle schools to get parental consent before changing a student's gender markers, pronouns, preferred name, or sex-based accommodations such as bathrooms and locker rooms, as a condition of receiving certain federal education funds.

2026-188.name: Smithsonian American Women's History Museum Act
2026-188.plain: The House voted on whether to pass a bill to create a Smithsonian women's history museum on a National Mall site and limit its focus to biological women. The bill failed, 204 to 216.

2026-19.name: Flexibility for Workers Education Act
2026-19.plain: The House voted on whether to pass a bill that would exclude voluntary training held outside regular working hours from counting as hours worked under federal wage law, if employees who skip it face no penalty and do no work during it. The bill failed, 209 in favor to 215 against.

2026-190.name: Veterans Gun Background Check Limits
2026-190.plain: The House passed a bill, 216 to 201, that would stop the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending veterans' personal information to the national gun background check system just because someone manages their benefits for them. Exceptions apply if a court finds the veteran is a danger to themselves or others.

2026-191.name: Veterans Benefits Expansion Act
2026-191.plain: The House passed a bill to expand benefits for veterans and their survivors, including a new monthly allowance for certain disabled veterans, larger survivor payments, and expanded VA home loan eligibility for some reserve and National Guard members. The vote was 235 to 179.

2026-192.name: Battlefield Preservation Grants Extension
2026-192.plain: The House passed a bill extending federal grants through 2036 to help preserve U.S. battlefields and to study sites from the French and Indian War and the Mexican-American War for possible preservation. The vote was 404 in favor and 13 against.

2026-193.name: Alaska Native Marine Mammal Products Act
2026-193.plain: The House voted 404 to 14 to pass a bill preventing states from banning marine mammal ivory, bone, or baleen legally made by Alaska Natives as traditional handicrafts and clothing.

2026-196.name: Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Act
2026-196.plain: The House passed a bill to extend for seven years a program that protects and restores marine waters, habitats and species in the Northwest Straits region of Washington state, by a vote of 374 to 49.

2026-198.name: Child Care Program Sanctions Bill
2026-198.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 207, that would require the federal government to impose additional penalties, including cutting off funds, on states that substantially fail to follow rules for the federal child care grant program for low-income working families.

2026-199.name: Removing Forces from Hostilities with Iran
2026-199.plain: The House approved a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress or a declaration of war authorizes them. Forces needed to defend the U.S., an ally, or a partner from imminent attack are exempt if the President follows the War Powers Resolution.

2026-200.name: Ukraine Support Act Floor Procedure
2026-200.plain: The House voted 218 to 204 to bring the Ukraine Support Act (H.R. 2913) to the House floor for debate. The bill would authorize support for Ukraine, and the House would send a message to the Senate that it passed the bill within one week of passage.

2026-201.name: Ordering Troops Out of Lebanon
2026-201.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from Lebanon within seven days. The resolution failed, 92 in favor and 324 against.

2026-203.name: Fast-Track Rule for Budget Reconciliation Bill
2026-203.plain: The House voted 213 to 211 to approve a procedural resolution that lets it consider certain rule reports on the same day without a two-thirds vote, through June 5, 2026. The change relates to a budget reconciliation measure.

2026-205.name: Agriculture and FDA Spending Bill
2026-205.plain: The House passed the bill by a vote of 213 to 210. It provides funding for the Department of Agriculture, the Food and Drug Administration, and related agencies for 2027, covering farm programs, food nutrition assistance, and rural development.

2026-207.name: Ukraine Support Act
2026-207.plain: The House passed a bill to help Ukraine and some European countries affected by the war with Russia, and to set penalties on Russia. The measure would fund Ukraine's reconstruction, allow certain military support, and impose sanctions and higher tariffs on Russia if the President finds it is waging war or refusing peace. The vote was 226 in favor and 195 against.

2026-208.name: TRUE Accountability Act
2026-208.plain: The House passed the TRUE Accountability Act, 384 to 0. The bill would require federal agencies to plan for preventing fraud and improper payments in emergency spending, such as money for disasters or pandemics, and to report those plans to Congress.

2026-209.name: Federal Fraud Prevention Workforce Training Act
2026-209.plain: The House passed a bill requiring federal employees who oversee federal programs or grants to take antifraud and improper-payment training every two years, with the program also offered to state, local, and tribal governments. The vote was 393 in favor and none against.

2026-212.name: Speeding Up Union Contract Negotiations
2026-212.plain: The House voted 220 to 199 to bring a bill to the floor that would speed up how quickly workers and employers must reach union contracts under federal labor law. Nearly all Democrats supported it, and nearly all Republicans opposed it.

2026-214.name: Secure America Act Funding Bill
2026-214.plain: The House passed the Secure America Act by 214 to 212. The bill provides about $70 billion through 2029 for border security, immigration enforcement, and related work by Homeland Security, Customs and Border Protection, and Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

2026-216.name: Faster Labor Contracts Act
2026-216.plain: The House passed a bill, 230 to 193, that would set deadlines for employers and newly recognized unions to reach a first contract, with mediation and binding arbitration if talks stall.

2026-217.name: Student Aid Identity Fraud Checks Bill
2026-217.plain: The House voted 249 to 172 to pass a bill requiring the Education Department to set up a system to detect possible identity fraud on federal student aid applications. Flagged applicants would need their identity verified in person or by live video before their aid is paid out.

2026-218.name: Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act
2026-218.plain: The House voted to pass the Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act, 240 to 181. The bill would give the Treasury Department's Bureau of the Fiscal Service new duties to prevent improper payments and create a Treasury inspector general office to audit and investigate federal funds, including pandemic and disaster spending.

2026-220.name: Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act
2026-220.plain: The House passed a bill, 218 to 200, to require federal agencies to temporarily hold or review payment requests that show a high risk of fraud or improper payment, and to shield federal employees from personal liability for good-faith actions under the bill.

2026-221.name: Extension of Foreign Surveillance Authority
2026-221.plain: The House voted on a fast-track bill to extend, until July 2, 2026, the government's authority to collect communications of non-U.S. persons abroad for foreign intelligence. The bill failed, with 198 in favor and 218 opposed, short of the two-thirds needed under this process.

2026-222.name: Condemning Government Fraud and Improper Payments
2026-222.plain: The House approved a non-binding resolution condemning people who try to defraud the federal government. It also expresses the view that fraud-prevention reforms would help the country's finances and that eligibility for federal programs should be checked before payments are made. The vote was 235 in favor and 177 against.

2026-223.name: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act
2026-223.plain: The House passed a bill, 368 to 19, that expands emergency aid for farmers and private forest owners hit by natural disasters. It lets them get advance payments for repairs and replacements, gives them 180 days to use the funds, and widens eligibility to include some wildfire damage.

2026-224.name: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
2026-224.plain: The House voted 358 to 32 to pass the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which changes federal housing programs. The measure includes changes to housing counseling oversight, grants for affordable housing and zoning guidance, and environmental review rules for some housing projects.

2026-225.name: Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act
2026-225.plain: The House passed a bill requiring Small Business Administration employees who handle its loans to certify in writing that they have no conflict of interest, and to disclose any conflict that arises later. The vote was 415 in favor and none against.

2026-226.name: Small Business Technology Loans Bill
2026-226.plain: The House passed a bill, 414 to 4, that would let the Small Business Administration guarantee loans under its main business loan program for software and cloud computing services that help businesses run operations, process payroll, manage sales and inventory, and use artificial intelligence tools.

2026-227.name: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act
2026-227.plain: The House passed a bill, 414 to 2, letting investment companies and their agents temporarily delay certain fund redemptions when they reasonably believe an older adult or a person with an impairment is being financially exploited. The delay can last up to 25 days, extendable by a state regulator, agency, or court.

2026-228.name: KIDS Act: Online Safety for Minors
2026-228.plain: The House passed the KIDS Act, 267 to 117, under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support. The bill would require websites with mostly adult content to block minors, give parents tools on social media and video games, and make AI chatbots tell minors they are not human and share crisis hotline information.

2026-229.name: Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Extension
2026-229.plain: The House passed a bill extending the federal program that shares losses with private insurers for terrorism-related damage through 2034. It also raises the loss threshold that triggers the program starting in 2029 and requires the Treasury Department to publicly explain how it decides whether an attack counts as terrorism.

2026-23.name: SHOWER Act (Showerhead Definition)
2026-23.plain: The House voted to pass the SHOWER Act, which sets a new legal definition of showerhead for federal water-efficiency rules and requires the Department of Energy to update its regulations to match. The bill passed 226 to 197.

2026-232.name: Ordering Troops Out of Lebanon
2026-232.plain: The House voted on a measure directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from fighting in Lebanon within seven days. It did not pass, with 189 in favor and 235 opposed. The measure would not limit support for Lebanese armed forces or protection of diplomatic sites.

2026-233.name: Ethics Committee Records on Harassment Settlements
2026-233.plain: The House voted to approve a resolution directing the Ethics Committee to keep and publicly release records of money settlements involving sexual harassment. The measure passed 420 to 0, with support from both Republicans and Democrats.

2026-234.name: Cold Weather Terrorism Preparedness Bill
2026-234.plain: The House passed a bill by 400 to 7 requiring the Department of Homeland Security to run an exercise preparing for a terrorist attack during extreme cold weather that disrupts critical infrastructure, then report the findings to Congress within 60 days.

2026-235.name: Easier Airport Security Screening for Families with Young Children
2026-235.plain: The House voted to pass a bill of 398 to 12 that directs the TSA to test alternative airport security lanes for travelers with children 12 and under, starting at no fewer than five airports, with priority for busy ones.

2026-238.name: Permanent Daylight Saving Time Bill
2026-238.plain: The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act of 2025, 308 to 117. The bill would make daylight saving time the permanent standard time, and states with areas exempt from daylight saving time could choose standard time for those areas.

2026-240.name: Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act
2026-240.plain: The House passed the bill 221 to 201. It would bar payment card networks from using merchant codes that single out firearms retailers from general-merchandise or sporting-goods retailers, and would have the Department of Justice enforce it and report on cases each year.

2026-241.name: Foreign Affairs and National Security Spending Bill
2026-241.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to a bill funding the State Department, foreign aid, and related national security programs for 2027. The amendment was rejected, 348 to 79.

2026-242.name: Funding for State Department and National Security Programs
2026-242.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to a bill that sets funding for State Department, national security, and related programs for 2027. The amendment was rejected, 247 to 178.

2026-243.name: Foreign Aid and State Department Funding Bill
2026-243.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to a bill funding national security, the State Department, and related foreign programs for fiscal 2027. The amendment was rejected, 314 to 104.

2026-244.name: National Security and State Department Funding Bill
2026-244.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the bill funding national security, the State Department, and related programs for the 2027 fiscal year. The House rejected the amendment, 421 to 6, so it was not added to the bill.

2026-245.name: Funding for State Department and National Security Programs
2026-245.plain: The House voted on an amendment to a bill that sets yearly funding for State Department operations, national security, and related programs for fiscal year 2027. The amendment was rejected, 136 in favor and 291 against.

2026-247.name: State Department and National Security Funding for 2027
2026-247.plain: The House voted 217 to 209 to pass a bill providing funding for the State Department, national security programs, and related foreign affairs agencies and commissions for the 2027 budget year.

2026-248.name: Naming Marietta VA Clinic for Colonel Michael H. Boyce
2026-248.plain: The House voted 418 to 0 to pass a bill naming the Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic in Marietta, Georgia, the Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic. The bill passed, with both parties voting in favor.

2026-250.name: Breast and Cervical Cancer Programs Reauthorization
2026-250.plain: The House passed a bill renewing federal programs on breast and cervical cancer screening, treatment grants for uninsured or low-income people, and education for young women about breast health, through 2030 and 2031. The vote was 394 in favor and 6 against.

2026-251.name: Penalizing Fraudulent Providers in Federal Workers' Injury Program
2026-251.plain: The House voted 396 to 0 to pass a bill letting the Labor Department stop paying providers convicted of fraud in the federal workers' compensation program, or in similar state or federal health programs such as Medicare. The Labor Department would also write the rules for carrying it out.

2026-252.name: Value Over Cost Act
2026-252.plain: The House passed a bill letting federal agencies buy through the General Services Administration's pre-approved supplier contracts based on overall benefit, not only the lowest price, when the agency decides that serves the government's interests. The vote was 421 in favor and 1 against.

2026-255.name: Amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act
2026-255.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the annual defense spending bill, which sets policy and authorizes funding for military programs. The amendment was rejected, 65 in favor to 361 against.

2026-256.name: Annual Defense Spending and Policy Bill Amendment
2026-256.plain: The House voted on an amendment to the annual defense bill, which sets policy and authorizes spending for the military and related national security programs. The amendment was rejected, 61 in favor and 360 opposed.

2026-257.name: Annual Defense Policy Bill Amendment
2026-257.plain: The House rejected a proposed change to the annual defense policy bill, 65 in favor and 359 against. The bill sets policies, equipment purchases, troop levels, and military construction for the Pentagon and related nuclear programs for fiscal year 2027.

2026-258.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2026-258.plain: The House approved an amendment to the annual defense spending bill by a vote of 265 to 161. The defense bill sets policy and authorizes funding for military programs, equipment, and personnel for the coming fiscal year.

2026-259.name: Defense Authorization Bill, Amendment Vote
2026-259.plain: The House voted on adding a change to the annual defense spending and policy bill, which sets rules for the military and authorizes equipment purchases and base construction. The change was rejected, 208 in favor and 219 against.

2026-26.name: Financial Services and National Security Spending Bill Amendment
2026-26.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to a bill that provides funding for the Treasury Department, the White House office, the courts, the District of Columbia, and the State Department and foreign aid programs. The amendment was rejected, 163 in favor to 257 against.

2026-260.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2026-260.plain: The House approved an amendment to the annual defense spending bill by 215 to 214. Its details are not stated in the official facts provided, so the bill's effect of this change cannot be described here.

2026-261.name: Amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act
2026-261.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the annual defense spending bill, which sets policy and authorizes funds for the military's programs, equipment, and construction. The amendment was rejected, 212 in favor and 216 against.

2026-262.name: Amendment to the 2027 Defense Authorization Bill
2026-262.plain: The House voted on adding an amendment to the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, which sets policy and spending authority for the military. The amendment was rejected, 201 in favor to 224 against.

2026-263.name: Annual Defense Spending Bill Amendment
2026-263.plain: The House rejected an amendment to the annual defense bill, which sets policy and authorizes equipment, ship and aircraft purchases, troop levels, and military construction for the coming year. The vote was 61 in favor and 365 against.

2026-264.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2026-264.plain: The House voted 350 to 76 to reject an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for fiscal year 2027. The bill sets Pentagon policy, spending, and military personnel levels for the year.

2026-265.name: Amendment to the 2027 Defense Authorization Bill
2026-265.plain: The House voted 215 to 214 to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, a bill setting policy and spending authority for military programs. The amendment was approved.

2026-266.name: Amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act
2026-266.plain: The House rejected a proposed change to the annual defense spending and policy bill, with 212 voting yes and 217 voting no. The change would have been added to the bill had it passed.

2026-267.name: Amendment to the 2027 Defense Bill
2026-267.plain: The House voted 219 to 208 to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, which sets policy and spending authority for military programs and equipment.

2026-268.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2026-268.plain: The House approved an amendment to the annual defense spending bill by a vote of 221 to 203. The bill sets policy and funding for the military, including weapons purchases, troop levels, and military construction.

2026-269.name: Amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act
2026-269.plain: The House rejected a proposed change to the annual defense spending and policy bill. The amendment failed 214 to 216, with nearly all Republicans in favor and nearly all Democrats opposed.

2026-27.name: Financial Services and National Security Appropriations Act, 2026 Amendment
2026-27.plain: The House rejected an amendment to the Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State appropriations bill, which provides 2026 funding for the Treasury, the White House office, the courts, the District of Columbia, and foreign affairs and aid programs. The vote was 127 in favor and 291 against.

2026-271.name: Main Street Capital Access Act
2026-271.plain: The House passed the Main Street Capital Access Act, 270 to 155. The bill would loosen many banking rules, including easing bank merger requirements and raising the asset thresholds that trigger fees, reports, and regulatory reviews, so more banks are exempt.

2026-272.name: Continuing Funding to Prevent Government Shutdown
2026-272.plain: The House passed a bill, 220 to 205, to keep federal agencies funded at current levels through December 4, 2026, preventing a shutdown when the new fiscal year begins. It also extends several expiring programs, including the National Flood Insurance Program and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families.

2026-273.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Act
2026-273.plain: The House voted 221 to 210 to add an amendment to the annual defense spending bill, which sets policy and funding authority for the military for fiscal year 2027.

2026-274.name: Amendment to the Defense Authorization Bill
2026-274.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, which sets policy and funding authorities for military and national security programs. The amendment was rejected, 207 in favor to 224 against.

2026-275.name: Amendment to the 2027 Defense Authorization Act
2026-275.plain: The House voted 232 to 199 to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, which sets policy and funding authorities for military programs, equipment, personnel, and related national security work.

2026-276.name: National Defense Authorization Act Amendment
2026-276.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for 2027, which sets policy and funding for military programs. The amendment failed, 175 for and 254 against.

2026-278.name: National Defense Authorization Act for 2027
2026-278.plain: The House passed the annual defense spending bill for fiscal year 2027, 216 to 212. It sets policy and funding levels for military programs, equipment, personnel, and related national security work.

2026-28.name: Financial Services, General Government, and National Security Spending Bill
2026-28.plain: The House passed a bill providing funding for 2026 to several federal departments and agencies, including the Treasury, the White House office, the courts, the District of Columbia, and the State Department and foreign aid programs. The vote was 341 in favor and 79 against.

2026-280.name: Stop Insider Trading Act
2026-280.plain: The House passed a bill that would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and require public notice before they sell them. The vote was 232 in favor and 198 against.

2026-281.name: Federal Budget Blueprint for 2027
2026-281.plain: The House approved a resolution setting the federal government's budget plan for fiscal year 2027 and outlining spending and revenue targets through 2036. The vote was 216 in favor and 214 against, and the plan directs several committees to draft legislation that would increase the deficit.

2026-282.name: Resolution to Remove Forces from Iran Hostilities
2026-282.plain: The House approved a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or authorizes military force. It would not stop the U.S. from defending itself or allies from imminent attack. The vote was 214 to 208.

2026-283.name: Disability Benefits Work Programs Bill
2026-283.plain: The House passed a bill extending for several years the Social Security Administration's authority to run pilot projects that help people on disability benefits work, with added rules on income protection, funding, and advance reporting to Congress. The vote was 232 in favor and 188 against.

2026-284.name: Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act
2026-284.plain: The House voted to pass a bill requiring the Justice Department to set national standards to prevent and punish sexual harassment and assault of federal prison staff by incarcerated people, and to carry out the recommendations of a Justice Department Inspector General report on the issue. The bill passed 376 to 8.

2026-285.name: Local Access to Courts Act
2026-285.plain: The House passed a bill, 378 to 10, that would require federal court sessions to be held in College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California. It was considered under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2026-286.name: Government Funding Extension Bill
2026-286.plain: The House voted 370 to 48 to accept the Senate's version of a bill that keeps federal agencies funded through December 11, 2026 and extends a range of expiring programs, including grain inspection, cybersecurity sharing, and trade preferences for African countries.

2026-289.name: Resolution Condemning Socialism
2026-289.plain: The House voted 220 to 192 to approve a resolution condemning and denouncing socialism in all its forms, opposing socialist policies in the United States, backing the SAVE America Act, and saying American elections are for American citizens only. Republicans voted yes and Democrats voted no, with 8 Democrats voting yes.

2026-29.name: Amendment to the Retirement Savings Investment Bill
2026-29.plain: The House approved an amendment to a bill on how retirement plan managers choose investments, by a vote of 395 to 22. The bill generally requires plan managers to base investment decisions mainly on financial factors that affect risk or return.

2026-291.name: Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act
2026-291.plain: The House voted to pass a bill delaying until 2035 the deadline for federal rules protecting endangered Atlantic large whales from lobster and crab fishing gear. The bill passed 219 to 196.

2026-292.name: Censure of Representative Chuck Edwards
2026-292.plain: The House voted 413 to 2 to approve a resolution censuring Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. A censure is a formal statement of disapproval by the House.

2026-293.name: Constitutional Amendment Setting Nine Supreme Court Justices
2026-293.plain: The House voted on a proposal to amend the Constitution so the Supreme Court would have nine justices. The measure failed to pass, with 212 voting yes and 206 voting no, short of the two-thirds majority required.

2026-294.name: Protecting Domestic Mining Act
2026-294.plain: The House voted to pass a bill that would let federal agencies use an expedited environmental review process for certain mining infrastructure projects, and would block a proposed rule that would narrow which mining projects qualify. The bill passed 218 to 201.

2026-295.name: Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act
2026-295.plain: The House passed a bill, 237 to 169, that would bar colleges receiving federal student aid from boycotting Israel without a valid business reason. It would also require colleges getting certain federal international education funds to certify that students and faculty can join academic programs in Israel on the same terms as programs in other countries.

2026-296.name: Invasive Species Strike Team Act
2026-296.plain: The House passed a bill, 371 to 33, that would formally authorize a federal program in which teams work with public and private groups to tackle invasive species on and around National Wildlife Refuges. The bill also requires the Fish and Wildlife Service to report to Congress on the program's progress.

2026-297.name: Local Communities and Bird Habitat Stewardship Act
2026-297.plain: The House passed a bill that would give legal authority to a Fish and Wildlife Service program working with cities to help conserve birds that live in or migrate through urban areas, including grants to local groups and institutions. The vote was 345 in favor and 60 against.

2026-298.name: Motion to Table Impeachment of Donald Trump
2026-298.plain: The House voted 232 to 147 to set aside a resolution to impeach President Donald Trump, which would have charged him with abusing presidential power by letting ICE and CBP operate in violation of constitutional protections and undermining judicial oversight. Setting it aside ends the resolution.

2026-301.name: GUARD Act on Financial Fraud Against Older Americans
2026-301.plain: The House passed the GUARD Act, 414 to 7, under a fast-track process that required two-thirds support. The bill lets state, local, and tribal police use certain federal grant funds to investigate financial fraud, including scams against older people and cryptocurrency investment schemes, and it requires the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network to report on these crimes.

2026-302.name: Bill Requiring Federal Financial Agencies to Review Technology
2026-302.plain: The House voted 417 to 7 to pass a bill requiring eight federal financial agencies to review their technology and buying rules and report to Congress every five years.

2026-303.name: Whistleblower Protections for Federal Housing Contracts
2026-303.plain: The House voted to pass a bill extending whistleblower protections to employees of contractors and grant recipients working on Department of Housing and Urban Development projects, including contracts signed before the law took effect in 2013. The bill passed 424 to 0.

2026-304.name: Diesel Emissions Reduction Act of 2025
2026-304.plain: The House passed a bill, 343 to 79, to extend through 2029 a program that offers grants, rebates, or loans to replace diesel engines or add pollution controls to them. The bill was considered under a fast-track process requiring two-thirds support.

2026-305.name: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
2026-305.plain: The House passed a bill, 408 to 17, that would let people who lost money to theft involving fraud claim a tax deduction in the year the loss happened, extend refund deadlines, and waive the 10% penalty on certain early retirement withdrawals.

2026-306.name: California Ocean Vessel Pollution Rule Repeal
2026-306.plain: The House voted 216 to 211 to pass a measure that would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency's approval of California's rules limiting air pollution from ships docked at its ports. The approval would be nullified.

2026-307.name: Removing Troops from Iran Hostilities
2026-307.plain: The House approved a non-binding resolution, 220 to 204, directing the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes the action or a declaration of war. Forces defending the U.S., an ally, or a partner from imminent attack are exempt if the President follows the War Powers Resolution.

2026-308.name: Russia and Iran Sanctions Act
2026-308.plain: The House voted to accept changes the Senate made to this bill, and it passed 262 to 159. The bill adds sanctions and tariffs related to Russia, extends an Iran sanctions law through 2031, and expands a tax deduction for teacher expenses to early childhood educators.

2026-309.name: National Fraud Enforcement Division Act
2026-309.plain: The House passed a bill, 352 to 72, to give legal authority to a Justice Department division that investigates and prosecutes fraud against taxpayer dollars and taxpayer-funded programs. The division was created by the department in April 2026.

2026-31.name: Retirement Plan Investment Rules Bill
2026-31.plain: The House passed a bill, 213 to 205, that would require people managing employer retirement plans to base investment decisions mainly on financial factors, such as expected risk and return, and to act in the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries.

2026-310.name: PROOF Act on Fraud in Federal Programs
2026-310.plain: The House passed the PROOF Act, 217 to 207. The bill would require states to share information with the Justice Department to investigate fraud in programs such as Medicaid, SNAP food aid, and TANF cash assistance.

2026-311.name: Overturning California Harbor Craft Emissions Rule
2026-311.plain: The House voted 214 to 208 to pass a measure that would cancel the federal approval allowing California to enforce its own pollution standards for commercial harbor vessels such as fishing boats.

2026-312.name: Ratepayer Protection Act
2026-312.plain: The House passed a bill, 417 to 3, that would have states consider making large data centers, which use 100 megawatts or more at one site, pay the full added cost of power equipment needed to serve them, rather than passing that cost on to other electricity customers.

2026-313.name: Water Resources Development Act of 2026
2026-313.plain: The House passed a bill, 415 to 9, to authorize and modify U.S. Army Corps of Engineers water projects such as harbor maintenance, flood and storm damage reduction, shoreline protection, and dam rehabilitation. It also directs the Corps to create an office to speed up project delivery.

2026-314.name: Retirement Plan Stock Valuation Bill
2026-314.plain: The House passed a bill, 401 to 14, letting retirement plans that hold employer stock use valuations from independent appraisers when the shares have no public market. The bill was considered under a fast-track process that requires two-thirds support.

2026-315.name: Nuclear Fuel Recycling Licensing Bill
2026-315.plain: The House voted 397 to 2 to pass a bill directing the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to license future facilities that recycle spent nuclear fuel under a simpler set of rules with fewer licensing steps.

2026-316.name: American Enrichment Deployment Act
2026-316.plain: The House passed a bill allowing uranium enrichment facilities to be built before the Nuclear Regulatory Commission issues a license, with the vote 394 in favor and 3 against. The bill requires the Commission to issue or revise its rules within 180 days of enactment.

2026-317.name: Impeachment Referral of the Defense Secretary
2026-317.plain: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment of Defense Secretary Peter Hegseth to committee rather than decide it on the House floor. Sending it to committee sets the measure aside for now.

2026-32.name: Main Street Parity Act
2026-32.plain: The House voted 383 to 8 to pass the Main Street Parity Act. It would lower the required down payment, by 5% of the total cost, for certain Small Business Administration loans to small businesses for buying, building, converting, or expanding plants and land for limited or single-purpose properties.

2026-320.name: Veterans' Combat Disability Pay Bill Procedure
2026-320.plain: The House voted 245 to 175 to move a bill to the House floor for debate. The bill would let disabled military retirees with combat-related disabilities receive both their veterans' disability payments and their retired pay.

2026-321.name: Retirement Plan Investment Options for Charities and Schools
2026-321.plain: The House passed a bill, 295 to 128, letting retirement plans for employees of public schools, charities, and churches invest in pooled investment funds held by banks and trust companies, and in certain insurance company accounts.

2026-33.name: AI for Main Street Act
2026-33.plain: The House passed the AI for Main Street Act by 395 to 14. The bill would require Small Business Development Centers to help small businesses evaluate artificial intelligence, including sharing best practices for using it and guidance on using it to plan for unexpected circumstances.

2026-37.name: Pregnancy Centers Funding Through Temporary Assistance Program
2026-37.plain: The House voted 215 to 209 to pass a bill that would let states use Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funds for pregnancy centers. The centers would offer services such as counseling, pregnancy education, pregnancy tests, diapers, and baby clothes to mothers, fathers, and families.

2026-38.name: Lifting Mining Protections in Minnesota's Boundary Waters Region
2026-38.plain: The House voted 214 to 208 to pass the measure, which would end a 20-year ban on mineral and geothermal leasing across about 225,504 acres of national forest land in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, Minnesota.

2026-4.name: Rule for Consideration of H.R. 1834
2026-4.plain: The House voted 221 to 205 to approve a procedural rule that sets the terms for debating a bill on policy priorities meant to break the gridlock. The vote does not itself pass the bill.

2026-40.name: Rules for Consideration of Spending Bills
2026-40.plain: The House voted 427 to 0 to add an amendment that sets the rules for debating two bills, H.R. 7148 and H.R. 7147, which would provide funding for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026.

2026-42.name: Homeland Security Funding Act, 2026
2026-42.plain: The House passed a bill providing funding for most Department of Homeland Security agencies for 2026, excluding Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Border Patrol, by a vote of 220 to 207. It also includes provisions related to pay and approvals tied to a partial shutdown of the department that began in February 2026.

2026-43.name: Amendment to Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
2026-43.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, which funds several federal departments and agencies for the rest of fiscal year 2026. The amendment was rejected, 164 to 268.

2026-44.name: Amendment to Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
2026-44.plain: The House voted on whether to add an amendment to the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, which funds several federal departments through the rest of fiscal year 2026. The amendment was rejected, 136 in favor to 291 against.

2026-45.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
2026-45.plain: The House passed a bill, 341 to 88, that provides funding for several federal departments and agencies, including Defense, Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, Transportation, Housing, and the State Department, for the rest of fiscal year 2026. It also keeps Homeland Security funded at 2025 levels through February 13, 2026, and extends several expiring programs.

2026-47.name: Pregnant Students' Rights Act
2026-47.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 211, that would require colleges receiving federal student aid to tell students about resources and accommodations for carrying a pregnancy to term, and how to file a discrimination complaint.

2026-48.name: Removing U.S. Forces from Venezuela
2026-48.plain: The House voted on a resolution directing the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Venezuela unless Congress has declared war or authorized the use of military force there. The vote failed, 215 in favor and 215 against.

2026-49.name: Veterans Readiness and Employment Improvement Act
2026-49.plain: The House voted 402 to 2 to pass a bill that would remove the requirement that Department of Veterans Affairs counseling on college campuses be provided by VA counselors. The bill was considered under a fast-track process that skips amendments.

2026-5.name: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water; Interior and Environment Spending Bill
2026-5.plain: The House voted 375 to 47 to keep this part of a larger bill. The measure provides federal funding for 2026 to agencies covering commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water projects, public lands, and the environment.

2026-50.name: Ernest Peltz Accrued Veterans Benefits Act
2026-50.plain: The House passed a bill setting rules for paying a veteran's approved pension that was still unpaid when the veteran died. Payment would go first to a living spouse, then living children, then living dependent parents, then the estate, with a one-year deadline to apply. The vote was 405 in favor and 1 against.

2026-53.name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
2026-53.plain: The House voted 217 to 214 to accept the Senate's changes to this bill, which provides federal funding for several departments and agencies for the rest of the 2026 budget year. It also keeps Homeland Security funded at 2025 levels through February 13, 2026, and extends several expiring programs.

2026-55.name: Critical Mineral Dominance Act
2026-55.plain: The House passed the Critical Mineral Dominance Act, 224 to 195. The bill directs the Interior Department to speed up mining on federal land to strengthen the country's supply of key minerals.

2026-56.name: D.C. Income Tax Conformity Resolution
2026-56.plain: The House passed a measure to overturn a D.C. Council law that had decoupled D.C. tax rules from federal changes. The resolution would restore federal tax provisions for D.C., including a higher standard deduction, a deduction for taxpayers 65 and older, and deductions for tips and overtime pay. The vote was 215 to 210.

2026-57.name: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
2026-57.plain: The House passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, 390 to 9, under a fast-track process. The bill changes and creates a range of federal housing programs, including grants, pilot programs, and rules on environmental reviews and mortgages.

2026-58.name: PROTECT Taiwan Act
2026-58.plain: The House voted 395 to 2 to pass the PROTECT Taiwan Act. It would direct the U.S. to seek to keep Chinese representatives out of six international financial groups if the President tells Congress that China's actions threaten Taiwan and U.S. interests.

2026-6.name: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water; Interior and Environment Spending Bills
2026-6.plain: The House voted 419 to 6 to keep Divisions B and C of the bill in place. Together these sections provide federal funding for 2026 to agencies covering commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water projects, public lands, and the environment.

2026-64.name: Securing America's Critical Minerals Supply Act
2026-64.plain: The House voted 223 to 206 to pass this bill. It would require the Department of Energy to track and assess the supply of energy resources the country depends on and that could be disrupted, and to develop plans to strengthen those supply chains.

2026-65.name: Ending the National Emergency on Tariffs
2026-65.plain: The House voted 219 to 211 to pass a measure relating to the President's February 1, 2025 national emergency declaration. Most Democrats and 6 Republicans voted yes, while most Republicans voted no.

2026-67.name: Undersea Cable Protection Act
2026-67.plain: The House passed a bill, 218 to 212, that would stop the Commerce Department from requiring its own permits for work on undersea fiber optic cables in national marine sanctuaries when a state or federal agency has already approved that work.

2026-69.name: SAVE America Act: Proof of Citizenship and Photo ID for Voting
2026-69.plain: The House voted 218 to 213 to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections.

2026-7.name: Commerce, Justice, Science, Energy, Water and Interior Spending Bill
2026-7.plain: The House voted 397 to 28 to pass a bill providing 2026 federal funding for departments and agencies covering commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water projects, public lands, and the environment.

2026-70.name: Less-Lethal Weapons and Federal Firearms Laws
2026-70.plain: The House voted to pass a bill that would remove certain less-than-lethal projectile devices, such as some TASERs, from regulation under federal gun laws and require a federal agency to decide within 90 days whether a device qualifies. The bill passed 233 to 185.

2026-71.name: Information Quality Assurance Act of 2025
2026-71.plain: The House passed a bill, 362 to 1, requiring federal agencies to rely on the best available evidence for rules and guidance and to publish the key factual material behind them, with a chance for public comment.

2026-72.name: ROTOR Act (Aircraft Tracking and Safety)
2026-72.plain: The House voted on whether to pass the ROTOR Act, which would require more aircraft tracking equipment and expand oversight of certain military and government flights. The measure failed to pass, with 264 in favor and 133 against, short of the two-thirds needed under this fast-track process.

2026-76.name: Home Appliance Protection and Affordability Act
2026-76.plain: The House passed a bill, 217 to 190, that changes how the Department of Energy sets energy efficiency standards for household appliances, adding factors such as cost and availability to consider.

2026-78.name: Homeowner Energy Freedom Act
2026-78.plain: The House passed the Homeowner Energy Freedom Act, 210 to 199. The bill would end three Department of Energy programs: home electric rebates for lower- and middle-income households, contractor training grants for home energy efficiency, and help for states and localities adopting building energy codes. It would also cancel any unspent money for the rebates and building codes.

2026-8.name: Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act
2026-8.plain: The House voted on whether to override the President's veto of a bill that expands the Miccosukee Reserved Area to include Osceola Camp in Everglades National Park and directs protection of its structures from flooding. The override failed, with 236 voting yes and 188 voting no, short of the two-thirds needed.

2026-81.name: Tribal Trust Land Homeownership Act
2026-81.plain: The House passed a bill, 384 to 40, to speed up how the federal Bureau of Indian Affairs handles home and business mortgages and related paperwork on tribal trust land. It also creates a Realty Ombudsman position within the bureau.

2026-82.name: Tuition Rates for Territorial Students
2026-82.plain: The House voted 351 to 72 to pass a bill requiring public colleges that receive federal student aid to charge students from Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands no more than in-state tuition, if they are also U.S. nationals.

2026-83.name: Sexual Harassment Ethics Records Release Resolution
2026-83.plain: The House voted 357 to 65 to send a resolution to committee rather than decide it on the floor, which usually sets it aside. The resolution would have required the Ethics Committee to preserve records of sexual harassment and sexual assault investigations involving members and publicly release available reports within 60 days, with victims' and witnesses' personal information redacted.

2026-84.name: Reaffirming Iran as Largest State Sponsor of Terrorism
2026-84.plain: The House voted 372 to 53 to approve a resolution stating that it is U.S. policy that Iran continues to be the largest state sponsor of terrorism.

2026-85.name: Removing Armed Forces from Hostilities Against Iran
2026-85.plain: The House voted on whether to approve a resolution directing the President to end the use of U.S. armed forces in hostilities against Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized the use of military force for that purpose. The resolution failed, 212 in favor to 219 opposed. It would not stop the U.S. from defending itself against imminent attack.

2026-87.name: Homeland Security Funding Bill
2026-87.plain: The House voted 221 to 209 to pass a bill providing money for the Department of Homeland Security for the rest of fiscal year 2026, ending a partial shutdown of the department that began February 14, 2026. The bill also provides back pay to affected federal employees.

2026-88.name: MAWS Act: Blue Catfish Purchase Pilot
2026-88.plain: The House voted 320 to 66 to pass the MAWS Act, which would have the federal ocean and weather agency set up a pilot program to buy invasive blue catfish caught in the Chesapeake Bay area from fishermen and processors for use in pet food, animal feed, or fish feed. It would also require estimates of the catfish population first.

2026-89.name: Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act
2026-89.plain: The House passed a bill, 345 to 41, to extend and change federal programs that give competitive research and development awards to small businesses. Changes include security-risk reviews of applicants, limits on how many proposals a business can submit each year, and extra awards for certain critical technology areas.

2026-9.name: Arkansas Valley Conduit Repayment Bill
2026-9.plain: The House voted on whether to override the President's veto of a bill that would remove interest and extend the repayment period to 100 years for communities paying for the Arkansas Valley Conduit, a Colorado water pipeline. The override failed, with 248 voting yes and 177 voting no, so the veto stands.

2026-93.name: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act
2026-93.plain: The House passed this bill 215 to 202. It would bar the Fish and Wildlife Service, the Bureau of Land Management, and the Forest Service from banning or regulating lead ammunition and fishing tackle on federal land and water, with some exceptions.

2026-94.name: Deporting Fraudsters Act of 2026
2026-94.plain: The House passed a bill, 231 to 186, that would make certain public benefits fraud, such as fraud involving food assistance (SNAP), Social Security, or federally funded programs, and producing fake identification documents, grounds for barring or deporting non-U.S. nationals. It would also make those people ineligible for certain immigration relief.

2026-95.name: Constitutional Amendment Requiring a Balanced Federal Budget
2026-95.plain: The House voted on whether to send a proposed constitutional amendment requiring a balanced federal budget to the states, using a fast-track process that needed two-thirds of those voting. The measure failed, 211 in favor to 207 opposed.

2026-96.name: Federal Working Animal Protection Act
2026-96.plain: The House passed the bill 228 to 190. It would make non-U.S. nationals convicted of, or admitting to, harming animals used in law enforcement inadmissible and deportable.

2026-97.name: American Water Stewardship Act
2026-97.plain: The House passed the American Water Stewardship Act by 378 to 32. The bill extends several EPA water quality programs, including Great Lakes, Long Island Sound, Columbia River, estuary, and beach safety efforts, through 2031, and bars certain Clean Water Act funds from going to entities tied to foreign countries of concern.
